newsitem.title: USA: King's son to visit James Earl Ray. [CORRECTED 01:37 GMT 28/3]
newsitem.headline: King's son to visit James Earl Ray. [CORRECTED 01:37 GMT 28/3]

text.p: The son of Martin Luther King Jr. was scheduled to meet James Earl Ray on Thursday to ask the former small-time crook to either confess to his father's murder or say who did it, a spokesman for the Atlanta-based King Centre said.
Dexter Scott King was to spend about an hour with the ailing Ray in Nashville, where Ray has been serving a 99-year sentence for the 1968 assassination of the civil rights leader in Memphis.

King Centre spokesman Steve Klein said the meeting would take place in Ray's prison hospital room in the Lois Deberry Special Needs Facility at 10 a.m. CST. Ray, who claims he did not kill King, is dying from liver disease.
King was due to hold a press conference at 11 a.m.
"He just wants to have a face-to-face meeting with Mr. Ray and see if he can shed any light at all on some of the questions surrounding Mr. King's father's assassination," Klein said.
Another King family representative told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution that King's first question for Ray would be: "Did you kill my father?"

Ray confessed to the assassination after his arrest, but later recanted. Ray, now 69 (corrects from 68), claims he was the patsy in a larger conspiracy and has repeatedly asked Tennessee officials for a trial.

The King family has backed Ray's call for a trial, saying they do not believe the public was told the truth about the assassination. Dexter King and his mother, Coretta Scott King, testified on Ray's behalf at a hearing in Memphis last month.

After the hearing, a state court judge recommended that an appeals court consider whether modern-day ballistics tests should be conducted on the rifle allegedly used by Ray -- a move that could open the door to a trial.
Ray's lawyers say the tests would show that the gun was not the one that killed King, and show that he was set up as part of a larger plot.
